cases.intro: The four faults reported first, and the two found while fixing them.
cases.title: Repeated tap raises the quantity
cases.pre: Counter paired; at least one product on the shelf.

The result appears. Time it.

cases.title: The user id rule is enforced, and explained before it is broken
cases.pre: On the registration screen, at the field that asks for the business user id.
cases.data: Try: a 4-character id · a 30-character id · one with a space · one with a dot or slash.
steps: Read the field before typing anything.
⭐ It says the rule UP FRONT — the length allowed, and that spaces and special characters cannot be used because they are reserved.
Enter something too short (4 characters).
Refused, and the message says the minimum. It does not just go red.
Enter something too long (30 characters).
Refused, with the maximum stated.
Enter one containing a space.
⚠️ Refused — and the reason given is that the character is reserved, not merely "invalid".
Enter a valid one and continue.
Accepted.

That is why the length is bounded and the separators are reserved: a space or a dot in the middle would make a compound name that cannot be read back apart. ⭐ The rule is cheap to state and impossible to undo once somebody has registered, which is why it is checked here rather than discovered later.
